chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Fats Waller's sixteen-piece band jamming at the Three Deuces; Waller at the Howard Theatre
summary: Waller brought his whole big band, with Al Casey, to jam in the small club, and later Collins saw him led on stage drunk at the Howard Theatre.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: You mentioned also very, very briefly Fats Waller and a 16 piece band?
Tell me about Fats Waller's band.

Well, he carried a big band, and he played all of the big theatres at this time, you know. And this was during the thirties, you know, and why I mentioned it is because normally, you know, one guy will come in to jam, you know, or maybe two, but Fats brought his whole 16 piece band in to jam. They took up the table space there was so many of them. This was -- the Three Deuces was really a small club. And they were appearing at the theatre right around on Randolph, I forget. But they came by and I remember the guitarist was Al Casey, very fine guitarist, who later played with Teddy's band, Teddy Wilson's band. And what was it, Eugene Spencer -- I mean, whoever, whatever his band was at that time, you know. He had augmented his small group. He always kept a small group, but this time he had this big band. And they came and played all night, and the people who could get in there were just thrilled because he was quite an entertainer.

I never was around Fats too much. We played a theatre opposite him, the Howard Theatre in Washington, and after that and the one thing that impressed me then was they had to lead him on, he was so juiced, they would lead him on stage during the black out and sit him down and then the lights would come on with him sitting at the piano. And at the end of the show they would black it out and someone would go out and get
him, and lead him off stage. You know. But how he could perform, I don't know, but it was a beautiful performance. But he would have cases of gin back there, you know.
